original_value: Linguistic variables play a vital role in several qualitative decision environments, in which decision-makers assume several feasible linguistic values or criteria instead of a single term for an alternative or variable. The motivation for the use of words or sentences instead of numbers is that linguistic classification and characterizations are generally less precise than numerical ones. In this research article, we encourage the fuzzy linguistic approach and introduce the novel concept known as m-polar fuzzy linguistic variable (mFLV) to increase the affluence of linguistic variables based on m-polar fuzzy (mF) approach. An mF set is an effective concept for interpreting uncertainty and fuzziness. The concept of mFLV is more versatile and sensible for dealing with real-life problems, when data comes from qualitative and multipolar information. We also introduce an mF linguistic ELECTRE-I approach to solve multiple-criteria decision-making (MCDM) and multiple-criteria group decision-making (MCGDM) problems, where the evaluation of the alternatives under suitable linguistic values are determined by the decision-makers. Furthermore, we validate the efficiency of our proposed technique by applying it to real-life examples, such as the salary analysis of companies and by selecting a corrupt country. Finally, we develop an algorithm of our proposed approach, present its flow chart, and generate computer programming code.

result.paraphrase: Linguistic variables are central to many qualitative decision-making settings, where decision-makers use several possible linguistic values or criteria rather than a single term for an alternative or variable. The reason for preferring words or sentences over numbers is that linguistic classification and description are generally less exact than numerical ones. In this article, we support the fuzzy linguistic approach and introduce a new concept called the m-polar fuzzy linguistic variable (mFLV) to enrich linguistic variables using the m-polar fuzzy (mF) approach. The mF set is a powerful tool for representing uncertainty and fuzziness. The mFLV concept is more flexible and reasonable for addressing real-world problems when the data are qualitative and multipolar. We also present an mF linguistic ELECTRE-I method for solving multiple-criteria decision-making (MCDM) and multiple-criteria group decision-making (MCGDM) problems, in which the evaluation of alternatives under appropriate linguistic values is assigned by decision-makers. In addition, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique through real-life case studies, including company salary analysis and the selection of a corrupt country. Lastly, we develop an algorithm for the proposed approach, provide its flowchart, and produce computer programming code.
